value.body: The Diplomate of National Board (DNB) is a postgraduate medical qualification awarded by the National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS), an autonomous body under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. Training happens in NBEMS-accredited hospitals — private, corporate, government and district hospitals — rather than only in medical colleges.

items.label: Course length
items.note: Post-MBBS broad specialty; 2-year post-diploma DNB also exists

items.label: Awarding body
items.note: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

items.label: Entry
items.note: Post-MBBS seats allotted through MCC counselling, as reported

items.label: Assessment
items.value: Thesis + formative assessment + final theory and practical exam

value.title: How you get in
value.body: An MBBS recognised under the NMC Act, 2019, completed internship and a 'qualified' NEET-PG result. Post-MBBS DNB seats are filled through MCC counselling with no domicile requirement (as reported). Doctors working regularly in government organisations can apply for sponsored seats.

value.title: At a glance
items: DNB is recognised as a postgraduate qualification; for teaching posts, NMC rules can add conditions such as hospital bed strength or senior residency — check the current regulations.
Seat quality varies a lot: look at patient load, number of faculty, past exam results and the stipend actually paid.
The final exit exam is set centrally by NBEMS, and pass rates have historically been lower than many university MD/MS exams.
Hospital-based training can mean heavy clinical exposure in busy centres.
